risk_summary: Risk analysis for Brightline's CRM shortlist (Salesforce, HubSpot, Zoho) covering GDPR/data residency, vendor lock-in and exit cost, migration risk, hidden costs, and support. Net position: no vendor presents a compliance blocker; the dominant risks are economic, not legal. Salesforce carries the highest aggregate risk for a 40-person agency (lock-in, hidden cost, adoption); HubSpot's principal risk is contact-tier and seat-creep pricing; Zoho's is shallower support/partner depth in Ireland and module sprawl. Risk-adjusted, HubSpot mixed-seat and Zoho Enterprise remain the credible finalists, consistent with hop-1 findings.
gdpr_data_residency_risk: All three vendors offer EU hosting, Art. 28 DPAs, and SCCs for residual transfers, so GDPR is a manageable risk, not a differentiator-killer. HubSpot: EU data centre (Frankfurt, Google Cloud) selectable only at portal creation - choosing it later requires a portal migration, so this must be locked in on day one; built-in consent/cookie tooling is strongest of the three. Zoho: own EU data centres (Amsterdam primary, Dublin secondary) - Dublin replication is locally attractive for an Irish controller; privacy-first, ad-free business model lowers third-party-sharing exposure. Salesforce: Hyperforce EU (Frankfurt/Paris) with the most granular controls, but meaningful privacy features (Shield field-level encryption, extended audit trail) are paid add-ons; data residency must be specified at provisioning. Residual transfer risk: all three are US-headquartered, so some support/telemetry access from the US persists under SCCs + EU-US DPF; for an ad agency (no special-category data at scale) this is low residual risk. Brightline-side obligations are identical regardless of vendor: RoPA update, DPIA-lite, processor register entry, and consent basis for any ad-audience syncing (HubSpot/Meta audience sync makes Brightline joint controller for matched audiences - document it).
vendor_lockin_exit_costs: Salesforce: HIGHEST lock-in. Proprietary metadata model (Apex, Flows, custom objects) means config investment is non-portable; data export is straightforward (weekly export service) but process logic is a total loss on exit; multi-year contracts with auto-renewal uplift clauses (typically 7-10%/yr) and no mid-term seat reduction. Estimated exit cost after 2 years: EUR 15-30k of rework plus sunk admin investment. HubSpot: MODERATE lock-in. Clean CSV/API export of CRM objects, but marketing assets (workflows, email templates, attribution history) do not port; free-seat users create soft lock-in via daily-use habit. Estimated exit cost: EUR 8-15k. Zoho: LOWEST per-app lock-in for CRM alone, but Zoho One deliberately entangles CRM with Books/Desk/Campaigns - if Brightline adopts the bundle, exit cost approaches Salesforce-like breadth (many apps to replace at once). Estimated exit cost: EUR 5-10k (CRM only), EUR 15-25k (Zoho One). Mitigation for all: keep the ETL/warehouse layer (already budgeted EUR 200-800/mo) vendor-neutral so reporting history outlives the CRM.
migration_risk: Inbound migration (from spreadsheets/legacy tooling) is low-to-moderate for all three: contact/company/deal imports are commodity. Risk concentrates in (a) data hygiene - dedupe before import, not after; (b) historical activity/email threading, which rarely migrates cleanly anywhere; (c) HubSpot-specific: EU hosting decision is irreversible without portal rebuild; (d) Salesforce-specific: migration typically requires a partner (EUR 5-15k) and 8-12 weeks vs 2-4 weeks self-serve for HubSpot/Zoho, extending the period of dual-running and shadow spreadsheets. A phased rollout (pilot pod of 5-8 users before agency-wide cutover) cuts migration risk materially on any vendor.
hidden_cost_risk: Salesforce: SEVERE. Realistic TCO adds a part-time admin or partner retainer (EUR 10-25k/yr), ads connectors via AppExchange (EUR 1-5k/yr), Shield/audit add-ons if needed, and renewal uplifts - true year-2 cost plausibly EUR 95-110k vs EUR 79.2k list. HubSpot: MODERATE. Marketing Hub contact-tier pricing is the classic trap (costs scale with database size, and ad-audience syncing inflates marketing contacts); paid-seat creep from 15-20 toward 40 doubles spend to EUR 43.2k; mitigate with quarterly contact pruning and a seat-governance policy. Zoho: LOW-MODERATE. List price is honest, but expect EUR 2-6k one-off for Zoho Flow/Zapier glue, Analytics setup, and possibly a consultant week; Ultimate-tier upsell pressure if API limits bite. Universal: ETL layer EUR 2.4-9.6k/yr applies to all three and should be in the recommendation's TCO, not a footnote.
support_risk: Salesforce: Standard support is slow (2-day targets); Premier Success costs ~30% of net spend - effectively another hidden cost; strong Ireland partner ecosystem (Dublin is a Salesforce hub) partially offsets. HubSpot: Pro tier includes phone/email/chat support with good SLAs; HubSpot's EMEA HQ is in Dublin - local presence, events, and hiring pool are a genuine advantage for Brightline; large agency-partner ecosystem. Zoho: Weakest of the three - email-first support from EU/India teams, paid premium support tiers (Premium ~20-25% of licence) for faster response; thin Irish partner bench means dependence on an internal champion; mitigate by budgeting premium support year 1.

risk_register.risk: TCO blowout: admin/partner retainer, connectors, renewal uplifts push real cost to ~EUR 95-110k/yr at 40 seats
risk_register.mitigation: Exclude from recommendation at this headcount unless enterprise-scale process needs emerge; if chosen, cap contract at 1 year, negotiate uplift ceiling, fix connector costs pre-signature.

risk_register.risk: Adoption failure / shelfware: HIGH learning curve, no in-house Salesforce skills at a 40-person agency
risk_register.mitigation: Pilot pod with success criteria before full rollout; budget formal training; do not customise beyond standard objects in year 1.

risk_register.risk: Proprietary config lock-in: Apex/Flow logic non-portable; exit rework EUR 15-30k
risk_register.mitigation: Keep business logic in the neutral ETL/warehouse layer where possible; document processes outside the platform.

risk_register.risk: Marketing contact-tier cost creep: database growth and ad-audience syncs inflate Marketing Hub fees unpredictably
risk_register.mitigation: Quarterly contact pruning policy; mark non-marketing contacts; alert at 80% of tier; revisit tier before each renewal.

risk_register.risk: Seat creep: drift from 15-20 paid seats to 40 doubles cost to EUR 43.2k/yr
risk_register.mitigation: Written seat-governance policy; free view-only seats by default; quarterly seat audit owned by ops lead.

risk_register.risk: EU data residency must be selected at portal creation; irreversible without portal migration
risk_register.mitigation: Make Frankfurt EU DC selection an explicit, checklisted step on day 1 of provisioning; verify in account settings before any data import.

risk_register.risk: Support and partner depth: email-first support, thin Irish partner bench, reliance on internal champion
risk_register.mitigation: Buy premium support for year 1 (~20-25% of licence, still cheapest TCO); nominate and train a named internal champion plus deputy.

risk_register.risk: Module sprawl / Zoho One entanglement raises future exit breadth and confuses users
risk_register.mitigation: Start with CRM Enterprise only; adopt additional Zoho apps deliberately, one per quarter, only against a stated need.

risk_register.risk: Shallow Meta/GA4 native integrations require Zoho Flow/Zapier glue that can silently break
risk_register.mitigation: Route ad-platform reporting through the neutral ETL layer rather than point integrations; add sync-failure alerting.

risk_register.risk: US headquarters: residual US access to support telemetry under SCCs/DPF despite EU hosting
risk_register.mitigation: Rely on SCCs + EU-US DPF certification; record in RoPA/transfer impact assessment; avoid storing special-category data in CRM.

risk_register.risk: Joint-controller exposure when syncing CRM audiences to Meta/Google for matched advertising
risk_register.mitigation: Document lawful basis (consent for audience syncing), update privacy notice, use platform joint-controller addenda.

risk_register.risk: Dirty-data migration: duplicates and dead contacts imported wholesale poison adoption and inflate HubSpot contact tiers
risk_register.mitigation: Dedupe and archive before import; migrate active pipeline only; keep legacy archive read-only in the warehouse.

risk_register.risk: Pricing basis risk: all figures are knowledge-cutoff (early 2026) list prices, +/-10-15%
risk_register.mitigation: Validate against live vendor quotes before contracting; treat hop-1 figures as planning numbers with 15% contingency.

risk_adjusted_recommendation_input: Risk-weighted ranking for the final recommendation: (1) HubSpot mixed-seat - lowest combined adoption+support+migration risk; manageable cost risks if contact/seat governance is instituted; Dublin EMEA HQ is a support advantage; lock EU DC at signup. (2) Zoho CRM Enterprise - lowest price and lock-in, acceptable risk if year-1 premium support and a named champion are funded; best pure data-residency story (Dublin DC). (3) Salesforce - severity-5 hidden-cost risk plus severity-4 adoption and lock-in risks make it unrecommendable at 40 seats. Carry into the recommendation TCO: ETL layer EUR 2.4-9.6k/yr, 15% price contingency, year-1 support/training budget.
risk_assumptions: Assumptions: no special-category personal data processed in CRM; Brightline is sole controller for its own pipeline data; knowledge-cutoff (early 2026) vendor terms - EU-US Data Privacy Framework assumed still valid, SCC fallback in place at all three vendors; exit-cost estimates are knowledge-based planning ranges, not quotes; severity scale 1 (negligible) to 5 (critical). No web verification performed.
